policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV main text reads "to him that is joined with all the living", rendering the qere yechubbar (pual of chabar, "is joined"). The mapped textual_variant note confirms the distinction by relegating the ketiv yibchar ("who can choose?", and the related "who is exempted?") to "Another reading", i.e. not the one the translators rendered.
